account:
It is just after eight on day one, and I am in my office with the secretary for the morning appointment. My schedule includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and three o'clock tea at the neighbour's cottage. The secretary says she has not found the miller despite checking last evening and this morning. Freight and the neighbour are to relay our request for grain stocks and delivery records. I do not know why the miller was absent; it is not evidence of a problem by itself.

The unusual feature is how ordinary delivery enquiries have become rumours. The neighbour personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery, but reports of bridge or port changes and decorations had no firsthand confirmation. The baker reportedly knew of no celebration. These may simply be distorted accounts of Freight seeking delivery work, rather than any actual town project. I have neither announced nor authorized such changes.

The builder asked this morning for repair jobs. I have no confirmed damage reports, and he has agreed not to incur costs or start work without agreement. He will bring specific locations and details if reports reach him. No paid inspections, repairs, or other spending have been authorized. Yesterday's recorded treasury count was 128 emeralds, but income and expenses remain unverified. I should read the appointment book this morning, hear any correspondence, and keep the mill visit focused on establishing the actual grain and delivery situation rather than treating gossip as fact.
